subject: Renewal negotiation: multi-year price stabilizer & commit rework (OrchidAI)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@orchidai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal negotiation: multi-year price stabilizer & commit rework (OrchidAI)

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for a productive call yesterday. Per our discussion I wanted to put a concrete proposal on the table to make OrchidAI's renewal predictable while giving you room to grow into increased capacity. High-level ask: extend the current 12-month price stability in a way that protects you from near-term price moves while letting Redwood scale cost-effectively.

Proposal (initial):
- Term: 36 months with a 12-month explicit price hold on the generation SKU (no token price increases for months 0–12).
- Pricing: 10% discount off list for year 1 on committed usage, then fixed +3% step increases for years 2–3 (capped).
- Commit: move from 500M tokens/year to 800M tokens/year (annualized). Quarterly true-ups to smooth usage variance; ability to add burst pool credits.
- Bridging credits: a one-time credit equal to 10% of year-1 committed spend that can be applied to overage charges in the first 6 months post-renewal.
- SLA / credits: standard SLA credits to apply after investigation; we can discuss higher SLAs under Dedicated capacity.

Attachments: draft term sheet attached for your procurement review (Redwood_Orchid_TermSheet_v1.pdf).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Procurement: review term sheet and return a list of redlines by next Wednesday (7/7).
2) Product/CS: coordinate capacity plan so we can confirm the commit is technically feasible without immediate Dedicated allocation.
3) Finance: I'll hold the renewal window open for 30 days while we iterate.

Open to swapping the smoothing approach — if OrchidAI needs a lower near-term commit we can explore a staged ramp with conditional credits. Let me know which path you prefer and I’ll get Ben and Marissa looped in with a revised term sheet.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: multi-year price stabilizer & commit rework (OrchidAI)

Jordan —

Thanks for the note and the draft. A few immediate items from procurement:
- Please provide a breakout of the list price basis (generation vs. embeddings vs. fine-tune) and the token definitions used in the commit number — we need that to map to our internal billing.
- We need clarity on invoicing cadence and whether credits are gross or net (i.e., applied before tax).
- Can you confirm you will pause any auto-renew functionality until the new terms are signed? Our legal team will not permit overlap.

Also: our cost-control team asked about a firm overage ceiling — what controls exist for burst usage that might spike us past the committed tokens in a single quarter?

I’ve looped Procurement on this message. We’ll aim to return an initial redline list by 7/8, but we may have questions before then.

Best,
Sara Lin
Head of Platform Operations | OrchidAI
sara.lin@orchidai.com

Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: multi-year price stabilizer & commit rework (OrchidAI)

Sara / Jordan —

Thanks for kicking this off. I reviewed Jordan's draft and put together an alternative that might better align with OrchidAI's usage profile and procurement asks:

Counterproposal (sales alternate):
- Term: 36 months; price hold months 0–18 if commit is increased to 900M tokens/year.
- Pricing ladder: 12% discount year 1 if 900M commit is agreed; otherwise 8% on an 800M commit. Yearly step increases capped at +2.5% thereafter.
- Onboarding / stabilization credit: $15,000 one-time credit applied to month 1 invoice to offset migration/QA costs.
- Bridging credit mechanism: credits vest monthly based on actual utilization vs. commit; unused credits expire after month 9.
- Overage guard: set a soft overage ceiling of 15% per quarter; usage above that triggers a trigger-review and temporary throttling options (we can agree non-disruptive throttling if you prefer).

I attached a revised term sheet that shows both the 800M and 900M paths and the math on year-1 economics (OrchidAI_Renewal_TermSheet_v2.pdf). Two quick asks from our side:
1) If procurement can confirm acceptable invoicing cadence (annual vs quarterly), we can finalize the credit timing.
2) Product/CS: we need to validate the feasibility of an 900M commit without moving to Dedicated GPU pools immediately — Jordan, looping Marissa for capacity input.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call with procurement and platform if that expedites things.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0160

Sara / team —

Quick product/CS note on capacity and the proposed commit uplift: we ran a light model on your Q1 peak profile and have a couple recommendations to avoid an immediate Dedicated footprint while supporting a higher commit: 

Operational mitigations we can deploy quickly:
- Prefix & KV cache tuning to lower peak inference token generation by up to ~22% on tail workloads.
- Request-level batching policy changes during known peak windows (we can route lower-priority async jobs to a burst pool).
- Instrumented usage gating: we propose a telemetry milestone (end of month 2) where we review real utilization vs commit; if utilization consistently exceeds 80% of commit in two consecutive quarters we revisit Dedicated allocation.

If we map the bridging credits to concrete milestones (e.g., 50% of onboarding credit released after verification of cache gains), it makes the economic trade easier for both sides. I dropped a short runbook into the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cOrchidRenewal — feel free to have your SREs look.

Happy to jump on the technical call with your platform team next week — suggest Wed 7/7 11:00–11:30 PT.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
